newsitem.title: MEXICO: Tribasa toll road trust bonds seen good buy.
newsitem.headline: Tribasa toll road trust bonds seen good buy.

text.p: Bear Stearns is recommending Mexico's Tribasa toll road trust bonds, saying they yield one of the highest spreads on any ten-year Mexican issue.

"Due to the Trust's recent revenue and cash flow growth trends, we recommend purchase of the Trust bonds, which offer the highest spread (736 basis points spread over U.S. Treasuries) of any ten-year Mexican issue," Bear Stearns debt analyst Mark S. Agnew said.
The bonds are guaranteed by net cash flow from two toll roads. They have a dollar price of 83, and a yield of 13.90 percent to a 9.83 year average life and a 5.19 year duration, Bear Stearns said.
There were $110 million worth of bonds issued on November 16, 1993.
"It is half way between a sovereign and a corporate. It is not backed by the government, but it is tied to the economy," said Agnew.
"The spread is wide and currently the cash flow just about matching interest expense," said Agnew. "But the growth in the traffic has been very good in the past few months."
